spec_fidelity_notes: Guard analysis (D, hitting sets, classes, identity flags, forced pairs) implements the docstring exactly. One divergence: the operation test labels UNTESTABLE when no pair has all 9 variables known, whereas the docstring says UNTESTABLE iff power==0 (power reported = 248); the power metric counts all cross-op opposite pairs and does not measure decisiveness. Minor wording: PARTIAL used when no pair is separable; model pools intersected with APPL not stated; independence emitted as list not number; legality 'PERFORMED or RULE' coded as ground!=CHOICE (equivalent on data).

identity_flag_assessment.reason: With exactly 2 opposite-outcome legality events, 'known values pairwise distinct' is equivalent to 'v separates the pair', so the flag duplicates FR (AUTHORIZE-IMPL a, OPEN-WORK k, REGISTER k, ASSIGN-ID h). It is also computed without reference to separation (fires on NEVER-SEPARATES SUPERSEDE a, e) and misses pair-level lookups (START t via git WP-4B/PERFORMED singleton; RAISE t in REV via ES-004.3/methodology singletons).
identity_flag_assessment.proposed_criterion: Cross-cluster value recurrence per forced pair: a separation of (p,q) by v is GENERALIZING only if p[v] recurs with p's outcome in another cluster and q[v] recurs with q's outcome in another cluster; LOOKUP if neither recurs, HALF-LOOKUP if one does. Add leave-one-cluster-out prediction for ops with >=3 clusters; ops with 2 events or 1 cluster reported INSUFFICIENT FOR GENERALIZATION instead of flagged.

disjoint_support._method: maximum matching of forced cluster pairs across all ops/variants/models where v is FR; within-cluster pair counts 1 (SCHEMA R4). START t: 5 distinct pairs, star on git-6a67da5d7 -> 1; START s: 4 distinct, R-58 hub -> 2; SUPERSEDE k: 2 distinct sharing ADR-MP -> 1.

supersede_scope_issue.detail: RESULT-1AM-SUPERSEDE uses 'SUPERSEDE mechanism by R-44 (reported in R-57)', absent from r4/OBSERVATIONS (only R-77, R-83, D-12 as legality events). With it, {r} and {a} conflict on (R-77, R-44), so r3's MF '{k} or {r}' is inconsistent with 1AM; only {k} can remain. Whether k separates (R-77,R-44) under r3 semantics is undecidable here (1AM used consistency-by-ignorance).
